summary: A tennis news roundup from December 2023. Nick Kyrgios escalated his feud with Boris Becker by mocking Becker's bankruptcy-related convictions after Becker said today's players owe a debt to past generations. The note also covers Tsonga's view on Djokovic, Hewitt captaining Australia at the United Cup, Corretja's doubts over a Djokovic Golden Slam, Pliskova on the WTA's lost charisma, and Murray's doubles pairing with Holger Rune in Brisbane.
one_line: Tennis news roundup: Kyrgios and Becker feud escalates, plus Djokovic, United Cup, Golden Slam doubts, Pliskova on WTA charisma, and Murray-Rune doubles.
key_facts: Nick Kyrgios escalated his feud with Boris Becker on X by raising Becker's bankruptcy-related charges; Becker spent eight months in prison in 2022.
Becker, a six-time Grand Slam winner, was found guilty of four charges under the Insolvency Act for hiding assets related to his bankruptcy.
The spat began when Kyrgios used Becker as an example of older players being poor pundits on modern tennis, and told The Athletic the game was 'so slow back then'.
Becker told Eurosport that players like Edberg, Wilander, Agassi and Sampras make it possible for Kyrgios to not play tennis all year and still make a living.
Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, a former world No.5, said Novak Djokovic went through a period of wanting to be Federer or Nadal and that he should have embraced his 'warrior' image as a Serb.
Djokovic told 60 Minutes he is not friends with Federer and Nadal because they are rivals, but hopes to be closer one day.
Lleyton Hewitt will captain Australia at the United Cup, with 18 nations competing in Perth and Sydney from December 29 to January 7.
David Witt, who led the United States to the 2023 United Cup trophy, returns for the Americans' title defence in 2024.
Alex Corretja questioned Djokovic's durability for a 2024 Golden Slam attempt, which would add the Paris Olympics to the four majors.
Djokovic ended 2023 as world No.1 for an eighth time but lost to Musetti, Rune, Alcaraz (Wimbledon final) and Sinner (ATP Finals group stage and Davis Cup).
Karolina Pliskova said the women's tour has lost charisma since the retirements of Serena Williams and Maria Sharapova, and that the WTA doesn't promote the game well.
Andy Murray added doubles at the Brisbane International with 20-year-old Holger Rune, a 16-year age gap; Murray slipped to world No.42 in 2023.
Holger Rune is world No.8 and coached by Boris Becker.
